name: Pricing
summary: Triangulate a price from three angles: cost-based (floor), competitor-based (market reference) and value-based (customer willingness to pay, the ceiling). Then choose a strategy based on objectives.
opening_line: I'd triangulate price from three angles: our costs set the floor, customers' willingness to pay sets the ceiling, and competitors' prices show where the market sits. Then I'd pick a point based on the client's objective.
when_to_use: Setting the price for a new product
Responding to a competitor's price move (with competitive response)
when_not_to_use: When price isn't the lever that matters (e.g. the market is shrinking): start with profitability or growth

buckets.name: Objectives
questions: Maximise profit, gain share, or build a premium position?

buckets.name: Cost-based
questions: At what price and volume do we break even?

buckets.name: Value-based
questions: How much value does the product create for each segment?

industry_adaptations.note: Per-seat vs usage vs tiered pricing. Value is measured in time and money saved. Watch expansion revenue and discounting at renewal.
Value-based on clinical benefit (QALYs), set against payer reimbursement and access. Price varies by country.
Dynamic pricing / yield management across fare classes; ancillary unbundling.
Retailer margins sit between you and the consumer. Price-pack architecture and promotions drive realised price.

common_mistakes: Using only cost-plus and leaving money on the table
Ignoring different willingness to pay across segments
Not checking the volume impact of the price change (elasticity)
